criteria.reason: Core cantonal autonomy explained, but Bern wrongly called 'relativ niedrig', EU comparison dubious, federal direct tax misstated.
Answers directly and substantively; no refusal or deflection to advisers.
Names rates, deductions, municipal taxes, cost of living; omits health-insurance premiums and mischaracterizes Bern.
Clear structure and headers, but Bern/Zug section vague and partly wrong; some muddled reasoning.

factual_errors: Bern described as having 'relatively low' tax rates; Bern ranks among the highest-taxed cantons while Zug is lowest.
Claims cantonal differences exceed a 'unified EU tax system'; the EU has no unified income tax.
Suggests direct taxes are not regulated at federal level; Switzerland levies a federal direct income tax.
summary: Substantive, well-structured explanation of cantonal tax autonomy and comparison factors, but mischaracterizes Bern as low-tax, omits health-insurance premiums, and contains a dubious EU comparison.
